design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks one layman's question — what do I owe, and let me pay it — and the answer is a
figure no field on the record carries. premium_balance_due reads 208.46; the notice she holds says
nothing she trusts; the true answer is 530.21. To reach it the representative must (a) notice that
the quarter now current has never been billed and rate it from the tier table rather than read it
off the ledger, (b) reconcile fifteen months of charges, payments, a part payment and an earlier
return, and (c) discover, from the policy's own rule and the member's Medicare Advantage record,
that the plan owes her a correction for a month on which both coverages stood in force, and book
that correction first. None of this comes from picking the right tool: both writes are named by the
policies themselves, and the difficulty is entirely in reading policy, querying the world and
getting the arithmetic right.

SCOPE: ALREADY OCCUPIED / CLAIMED HERE / RESERVED
This is the first task of the difficulty, so nothing was occupied before it. It claims the premium
side of the charter: medigap_ext_dual_coverage_premium_return (subject medigap_premium_refund,
target post_overlap_premium_return_c83152d2) and medigap_ext_premium_account_settlement (subject
medigap_premium_payment, target remit_supplement_settlement_23b5df61), resting on the base policies
medigap_premium_rating and medigap_premium_billing_and_posting. Reserved for task 1: the whole
claims side — medigap_benefit_payment and medigap_claim_adjustment_and_recovery, the crossover
tables, and the three problems of its tree (settling a pending crossover line, booking a recovery on
a line Medicare has restated, and the policyholder's own repayment of a benefit paid to her
directly). The two tasks share no policy, no task tool, no base subject event and no computed
quantity.

THE DRAW (Step 0, scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/medicare_supplement_policy_desk --task 0)
{"task": 0, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/0",
 "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}
The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem and two computations, one carrying six
factors and one carrying four. The root problem (the settlement) takes the six; the prerequisite
(the return) takes the four.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: medigap_ext_premium_account_settlement — the figure the caller asks for.
Prerequisite problem: medigap_ext_dual_coverage_premium_return.
Edge: settlement <- return, kind value_input, gate returns_credited (a compute binding of the
settlement), form state.
  Prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the settlement's own rule): "The amount a policyholder must
  pay to bring the account up to date is not fixed before the premium account carries the return
  owed on premium charged for months in which other Medicare coverage was still in force."
  Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result — the amount the policyholder must pay —
  to what it waits on with the ordering connective "not before", in the negated direction; the
  affirmative rewriting, "the amount is fixed only after the premium account carries the return
  owed ...", states the same dependency with the same result, the same waited-on state and the same
  scope, nothing added, dropped or split, and the negated form negates the whole of the waited-on
  condition rather than listing failure cases. The negated direction is the one this desk uses for
  a figure it will not quote until the account is square, which is how a premium desk speaks about
  money it is about to take. (2) The side it waits on is a record-visible state — a return entry
  standing on the premium account for premium charged for particular months — named in the words
  the premium account and its finder use; no action, no performer and no tool. (3) No tool name, no
  policy id, no snake_case token, no row id. (4) Its strength is exactly the edge's: a hard "not
  before", and the months are the closed set of months on which other Medicare coverage was still
  in force, neither wider nor narrower than the condition.
  State-form legality: exactly one write of this difficulty brings such an entry about,
  post_overlap_premium_return_c83152d2, the target tool of the dual-coverage return policy; no other
  policy of this charter books a return of premium.
  Derivation the reader must make: the sentence says the settlement waits on a return entry for
  premium charged for months of doubled cover. The premium account (find_medigap_premium_ledger)
  shows one return only, 7.18 on 2025-07-10, carrying the duplicate-payment reason and giving back
  the excess of an overpayment, so the state does not hold. Reading the other rule of this charter,
  the dual-coverage return policy says what such a return is and that its own result is the amount
  returned; its target tool is therefore the one write that brings the state about, and it must come
  first. That is one reading, not two.
  Handling-time condition: the premium account carries a return entry for the premium charged for
  the months in which the policyholder's other Medicare coverage was still in force.
  Resolving action and owner: post_overlap_premium_return_c83152d2, owner agent.
  Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.medigap_premium_ledger.586aaae6-0dcb-4823-8f9d-4683c4318f5a
  .refund_reason_code = duplicate_payment and .amount = 7.18 (the only return on the account);
  initial_state.medigap_premium_ledger.ff05814a-d82e-4d35-b392-91464b959dc7.amount = 452.82 (the June 2025 premium charge standing
  in full); initial_state.advantage_enrollments.36454f16-84ae-49a3-a773-0ebfc22ade70.coverage_end_date = 2025-06-30 against
  initial_state.medigap_policies.06781a6e-fabf-45b5-b4c5-ceccf58e670a.policy_effective_date = 2025-06-01.
  Topological order: return, then settlement. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the return
  leaves the settlement at 675.64 instead of 530.21.
  The customer's own write: the settlement is the policyholder's own act — remit_supplement_settlement_23b5df61
  is owner=user, unlocked and handed over by the representative at the root problem's place in the
  order, and run by her. In-person semantics: the money is hers, she says so ("the money is yours
  and you want to be the one who hands it over"), and a telephone payment completes on the spot.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Write subject medigap_premium_refund (the return). Governing base policy: medigap_premium_billing_and_posting.
Its two eligibility gates, policy_open_for_posting and payment_not_already_posted, both apply_to
medigap_premium_payment only, so neither governs this write; what is inherited is the policy's scope
— money is returned against a single named charge, and the refund names the charge it returns, which
the tool enforces by carrying source_premium_entry_id. No time gate.
Write subject medigap_premium_payment (the settlement). Governing base policy: the same.
  policy_open_for_posting: "The policy stands at active or grace_period on the day the charge is
  posted." Authoritative evidence: initial_state.medigap_policies.06781a6e-fabf-45b5-b4c5-ceccf58e670a.status = active, correlated
  to the action through medigap_policy_id. Satisfied at frozen_time; if the policy had lapsed the
  base rule would hold the money rather than post it, and no payment could be written.
  payment_not_already_posted: "No payment entry carrying the same remittance reference and the same
  amount is already posted on this policy." Authoritative evidence: the account's thirteen entries,
  none of which carries the reference PN-20260826-44713; the correlation key is the premium account
  entry the money is applied against, the June 2026 charge d3c3a20c-66fe-424b-b2f6-1a721d853891.
No base eligibility on either write is a time gate, so temporal_feasibility is empty. The base
counting rules that do bear on the figures — the due day of the first month of a span, and money
being posted against the oldest unpaid billing period first — are inherited unchanged and are what
fix billing_period on the payment.
Nothing in either extended policy contradicts a base sentence: the rating rule is applied exactly as
base states it (the tobacco and area factors multiply the base premium before any reduction, the
policy fee is added afterwards and is never discounted), so both policies declare overwrite: [].

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target object of the return: the single premium charge ff05814a-d82e-4d35-b392-91464b959dc7, posted 2025-06-01 for billing period
2025-06, 3 months of cover, 452.82, rate basis issue_age_table — the charge that paid for the month
of doubled cover. Correlation key: source_premium_entry_id on the new entry. Rows that enter its
arithmetic: ff05814a-d82e-4d35-b392-91464b959dc7 (the premium of the opening span), 580e7c87-a9f8-4be4-aca5-b59ac24e4d0f (the policy fee of the opening span, whose
share is returned with the premium) and 586aaae6-0dcb-4823-8f9d-4683c4318f5a (the 7.18 already returned). Rows excluded: every
charge of a later span, because the window that isolates the opening span is the months the policy
has been in force; and the opening payment c17fa1f4-098c-4d6f-a6a0-dc3786505efb, which is money in, not a return.
Target object of the settlement: the premium account of policy 06781a6e-fabf-45b5-b4c5-ceccf58e670a as a whole, applied against the
oldest unpaid billing period, the June 2026 charge d3c3a20c-66fe-424b-b2f6-1a721d853891. Rows included in the reach-back: 33386222-e369-4388-a3b1-a8ac926bba41,
33334196-96ca-482e-a616-c4b84cc2bff4, d3c3a20c-66fe-424b-b2f6-1a721d853891, 687bbddf-99fb-4738-a812-fe3829288a9f and the payments 79e7a83c-29bc-4f24-b02c-7b2191c8559b, a6320d3e-51f4-49a8-85b4-9579232a6ea1, 00bb4953-1b79-42d1-b2b8-f99f0ed31fd6. Rows excluded: ff05814a-d82e-4d35-b392-91464b959dc7, 580e7c87-a9f8-4be4-aca5-b59ac24e4d0f, 82ec0bd8-e3b0-44e8-9fd3-842c24be734f, c17fa1f4-098c-4d6f-a6a0-dc3786505efb, da128067-bb83-4107-9edf-55c43e69b61b and
586aaae6-0dcb-4823-8f9d-4683c4318f5a, all posted more than twelve months before the handling date — the near-miss is 82ec0bd8-e3b0-44e8-9fd3-842c24be734f and da128067-bb83-4107-9edf-55c43e69b61b
of 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-03, exactly twelve months back and therefore outside the twelve months to
date; a careless reconciliation that sweeps them in changes both the charges and the credits.
Settled objects: the spans 2025-06, 2025-09, 2025-12 and 2026-03 each carry a payment that settled
them (the opening span by an overpayment whose excess was returned), so the only span still standing
unpaid is 2026-06.

THE WORLD, ROW BY ROW, AND WHAT IT CARRIES
customers.211c920f-8004-4c4e-b71e-4f560d1262ca: the caller. Her date of birth fixes the issue age of 75 on the policy record;
remove it and the rating basis cannot be checked.
advantage_enrollments.36454f16-84ae-49a3-a773-0ebfc22ade70: the Medicare Advantage enrollment she left, coverage_effective_date
2023-01-01, coverage_end_date 2025-06-30, status disenrolled. This is the cross-difficulty evidence:
delete it and overlap_months falls to its fall-through of nil and the return falls to 0.00.
medigap_policies.06781a6e-fabf-45b5-b4c5-ceccf58e670a: Plan N, active, effective 2025-06-01, issue age 75, standard class, drawn by
bank transfer, billed quarterly. The cadence fixes the three months the current period covers; the
payment method is one limb of the reduction tier; the effective date fixes both the fifteen months
in force and the opening span.
medigap_underwriting_files.f64f0852-cdd7-487b-9c2a-511dad6a8d98: the application and the recorded decision accepted_standard, which
is why the rating class is standard and the tobacco factor does not bite. It also shows the
requested effective date of 2025-06-01 against the Medicare Advantage end date of 2025-06-30 — the
origin of the error the return corrects.
Ledger: ff05814a-d82e-4d35-b392-91464b959dc7/580e7c87-a9f8-4be4-aca5-b59ac24e4d0f the opening span and its policy fee; c17fa1f4-098c-4d6f-a6a0-dc3786505efb the 480.00 overpayment against it and
586aaae6-0dcb-4823-8f9d-4683c4318f5a the 7.18 already returned (which the return's own deduction tier reads); 82ec0bd8-e3b0-44e8-9fd3-842c24be734f/da128067-bb83-4107-9edf-55c43e69b61b the
September 2025 span, settled, and the near-miss at exactly twelve months; 33386222-e369-4388-a3b1-a8ac926bba41/79e7a83c-29bc-4f24-b02c-7b2191c8559b and 33334196-96ca-482e-a616-c4b84cc2bff4/a6320d3e-51f4-49a8-85b4-9579232a6ea1
the December 2025 and March 2026 spans, settled, and the two settling payments the reduction tier
counts; d3c3a20c-66fe-424b-b2f6-1a721d853891/687bbddf-99fb-4738-a812-fe3829288a9f the June 2026 span and the second policy year's fee, standing unpaid, and 00bb4953-1b79-42d1-b2b8-f99f0ed31fd6 the
250.00 cheque that leaves part of it unpaid and turns the credit tier off its fall-through.
No automatic clause of the base charter is lit by these rows: the policy is active and no premium is
overdue past its grace period (the June 2026 span was partly paid inside the grace period and the
plan has raised no grace-period entry), no claim exists to pay, and no rate review falls inside the
call. There is no stale cache in this task: premium_balance_due is exactly the ledger sum
(2304.10 - 2088.46 - 7.18 = 208.46), and the trap is not that the field is wrong but that it is a
different quantity from the one the caller is asking for.

PERSONA
Marguerite is written as a specific person — unhurried, apologetic, a folder on the kitchen table —
rather than as a list of facts, and the six kinds of information are woven into her narration: who
she is; the letter and the missing autumn bill; the object (her supplement policy) and the timing
(today, on this call); the authority boundary (she is happy for the representative to look at
anything, but she hands the money over herself); what she says only when asked (payment method, the
cheque, the earlier Advantage plan, the payment reference, how she wants to pay); and her passive
reactions (mild pleasure at a correction she is told about, running the payment when it is handed
to her, closing once it has gone through). She never names a figure that gold computes, never
mentions a return or a correction before she is told of one, and never corrects a representative who
goes wrong. Her arc ends exactly where evaluation_criteria ends: the last thing she does is make the
payment and read the confirmation back, and she asks for nothing beyond it.

THE PRERQUISITE CHAIN AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED
Surface goal (what do I owe) -> the settlement policy's rule -> the sentence that the figure is not
fixed before the account carries the return owed for months of doubled cover -> the premium account,
which shows no such return -> the dual-coverage return policy, whose write books it -> the Medicare
Advantage record, which fixes the months -> the opening span's entries, which value them -> the
return -> back to the settlement, whose returns_credited now reads 145.43. The order cannot be
swapped: the settlement's own binding reads the account at its handling time, so a settlement
written first is written on a world in which the return does not exist.
Breadth at the settlement: the tier table (base premium, issue-age step, area factor, policy fee,
electronic funds transfer reduction, annual payment discount), three separate history windows (the
twelve months to date for charges, payments and returns; the current quarter for the period now
current; the whole account for the largest payment span), the policy record (cadence, payment
method, issue age, rating class, effective date) and the negative space of the annual payment
discount, which is exactly what a policyholder paying a large sum at once might be expected to get
and does not.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT
 - Reading premium_balance_due (208.46) as the answer: the rule states what the settlement is built
   from, and the quarter now current is not in that figure at all.
 - Paying only the arrears (222.82): the rule's first sentence includes the premium owed for the
   billing period now current.
 - Billing the current quarter at 458.82 by forgetting the electronic funds transfer reduction, or
   at 364.02 by taking the base rate for a policyholder issued at 65.
 - Giving the annual payment discount because she is paying a large amount now: the tier asks for a
   payment covering twelve months of cover standing on the account, and the largest span any payment
   on this account carries is three months.
 - Sweeping in the September 2025 charge and payment, which fall exactly twelve months back and are
   outside the twelve months to date.
 - Adding a fee instalment of 5.00 when the policy year's fee entry already stands on the account.
 - Returning 152.61 for the doubled-cover month by ignoring the 7.18 already returned, or 447.31 by
   returning the whole opening charge rather than one month of it.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate and verify; read the policy, the premium account, the underwriting file and the Medicare
Advantage enrollment; see that the account carries no return for the doubled-cover month; work the
return out (1 month x (452.82/3 + 20.00/12) - 7.18 = 145.43) and book it against the June 2025
charge; then work the settlement out on the world that now includes it (452.82 + 1378.46 + 0.00 -
1155.64 - 145.43 = 530.21), tell the caller the figure, hand the telephone payment over to her, and
let her pay it against the oldest unpaid billing period, 2026-06, as an overpayment carrying the
reference from her letter.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5)
A probe built on the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py
build_env / eval_compute / substitute) was run over this initial_state at frozen_time, replaying the
return with the real task tool before evaluating the settlement:
  B result 145.43 touched 9 branches 13
     B factor coverage_overlap_months -> 0.0
     B factor opening_month_valuation -> 447.31
     B factor returned_rate_components -> 143.76
     B factor money_already_given_back -> 152.61
     B all-baseline 0.0
  A result 530.21 touched 10 branches 18
     A factor age_rating_basis -> 441.41
     A factor payment_method_reduction -> 536.21
     A factor current_period_valuation -> 77.39
     A factor arrears_reach -> 307.39
     A factor credit_for_money_received -> 780.21
     A factor policy_fee_due_with_settlement -> 535.21
     A all-baseline 0.0
  A without B -> 675.64   (the prerequisite-sensitivity run)
Every figure above is carried into computations.expected, factor_sensitivity and
edge_load_bearing unchanged, and the per-task gates recompute them.

RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding of both policies that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim
quotation in compute_basis, including the aggregation windows, the tier ladders, the acting base of
each multiplication, the order of operations and the single rounding at the end. Backward: reading
each rule through, the sentences carrying a quantity, window, filter, branch or rounding semantic
are all claimed — the cadence sentence by span_months, the rating sentences by
age_rated_monthly_premium and rated_monthly_premium, the reduction sentences by
monthly_premium_reduction, the current-period sentences by current_span_value, the reach-back
sentences by arrears_window_months and arrears_charges, the fee sentences by fee_instalment, the
credit sentences by credits_allowed, the return sentence by returns_credited and the closing
sentence by result; on the return policy, the months sentences by overlap_months, the valuation
sentences by monthly_premium_returned, the component sentences by monthly_component_addition, the
deduction sentences by return_offset and the closing sentence by result. No sentence is left
unclaimed and no filter in an expression is absent from the prose: the twelve months to date, the
billing period now current, the settles-balance and part-payment filters, the policy-fee rate basis
and the issue-age rate basis all appear in the rules in those words.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD
Both gold writes carry their business stage, their request binding and their base preconditions
above. The return cites only pre-action system evidence (the Advantage end date, the policy
effective date and the opening charge); the settlement cites the caller's own words for its intent
and the account rows for its object; every credential the verification uses appears verbatim in the
persona; and the only fact established during the call — the return entry — is cited as prior_step:7
rather than as something the caller asserted.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Setting the extended yaml, compute, expected and this dossier aside and working only from what a
rollout can see (the rules as they will be published, the tool schemas, what the finders return and
what the caller actually says), the same path falls out: the policy is Plan N, active, quarterly, by
bank transfer, effective 2025-06-01; the account has no charge for the quarter beginning September
2026, so that quarter is rated; the rated quarter is 452.82; the twelve months to date carry
1378.46 of charges and 1155.64 of credited money; the fee already stands; and the rule's own
sentence about waiting for the return sends the reader to the Advantage record, where the June 2025
overlap yields 145.43. 530.21 is the only figure that follows, and the posting flag can only be
overpayment because the account shows 63.03 outstanding once the return is booked.

GATES RUN, AND THE ONE DEFECT THE MANUAL REVIEW FOUND
Per-task scripts, all green on this task: check_extended --task 0 (EXTENDED OK), check_task_tools
(TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK), replay_tasks --task 0 (REPLAY OK, 10 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous,
closure 17 of 17 rows), check_solvability --task 0 (SOLVABILITY OK, 2 calls, 3 base gates, 14 seed
rows), check_compute --task 0 (COMPUTE OK, 2 computations, 10 factors, 1 cross-difficulty, 19
history rows, 31 branches), check_grounding --task 0 (GROUNDING OK), check_cross_fire --task 0
(SCOPE OK). check_cache_diff reports no cache trap in this task, which is correct: there is none.
Manual values gates then found one real defect no script sees. Symptom: three ladders had two tiers
that could both hold of the same customer as stated — the reduction ladder (a twelve-month payment
standing and bank transfer with two settling payments), the credit ladder (a part payment and an
overpayment), and, on the return policy, the rate-component ladder (a fee entry and a rate-increase
entry) and the deduction ladder (a return already paid and an overpayment standing, both of which
are in fact true of this very world). Root cause: the ternary chains in compute encoded the priority
while the prose did not state it, so the partition was an artefact of listing order. Change: the
second tier of each of those four ladders now carries the negative of the first in its own words
("where no payment covering twelve months of cover stands on the account ...", "where no payment
posted within that span left part of its billing period unpaid ...", "where no entry carrying the
policy fee stands for the opening span ...", "where no return has yet been paid on the policy's
premium account ..."), in the rule, in compute_basis and in the ladder. Re-run: check_extended
--task 0 and check_compute --task 0 both green again, with every expected value unchanged
(145.43 and 530.21), because the compute was already evaluating in that order.

REWORK ROUND 2 — CHARTER FINDINGS CLOSED (audits/policy_task/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/)
CG-1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, undeclared override: the household discount dropped). Symptom: base
medigap_premium_rating says "The household discount and the annual payment discount stack: both are
taken, one after the other, on the premium after the rating factors and before the policy fee",
while medigap_ext_premium_account_settlement declared overwrite: [] and its reduction ladder yielded
at most one reduction, never the household one. Root cause: the ladder was written as the whole of
the discounting rather than as the reduction for the way the policyholder pays, so a base branch had
no selector in the extended policy. Change (the honest business reading is to restore the branch,
not to override base): the rule now says the household discount is taken from the rated monthly
premium where the plan holds the policy as taking it, that the reduction for the way they pay is
then taken from what the household discount leaves, and that the two are taken one after the other
and never combined into a single rate; a new plumbing binding household_adjusted_monthly_premium
implements it from household_discount_applied and the tier's household_discount_percent; the annual
payment discount tier and the current-period valuation now act on that binding; the sentence is part
of baseline.rule and household_discount_percent is added to baseline.params. overwrite stays [] and
is now true. Re-run: EXTENDED OK, COMPUTE OK; every figure of this task is unchanged (145.43,
530.21, all ten factor baselines, the 0.00 fall-backs and the 675.64 skip-run), because this
policyholder's record holds household_discount_applied = none, so the restored branch evaluates to
the rated premium here. The defect is closed in the charter regardless of what this seed holds.
CG-4 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, "the credit standing from that overpayment" implemented as the whole
payment). Symptom: both premium-side policies promised a credit and summed the whole payment row
(480.00 where the credit was 7.18), because medigap_premium_ledger carries no excess field. Root
cause: the rule named a quantity the records do not carry. Change: both rules now name a quantity
the ledger does carry and both computes implement exactly that — in the return policy, "the amount
by which the money received exceeds the premium charged" (payments less charges on the account,
never below nothing); in the settlement policy, "the amount by which the money received within the
span exceeds the charges posted within it" (payments less charges inside the reach-back window). The
balance_effect='overpayment' filter is gone from both bindings; rule, compute_basis and the two
ladder tiers were changed together. Re-run: both tiers now agree with their prose on any world, not
only on one where a prior tier fires first; this task's figures are unchanged because the return
still takes the already-returned tier (7.18) and the settlement still takes the part-payment tier.
CG-5 belongs to task 1's policies and is recorded in that task's dossier. The observations (OBS-B
label, OBS-C degenerate baselines, OBS-D unrelated refunds netted, OBS-F hand-over arguments) were
not red lights and are left as the auditor recorded them.
user_scenario:
You are Marguerite Nieves, seventy-six, a retired school librarian living on SE Hazel Court in Gresham. You are unhurried and a little apologetic on the telephone, you say things twice when you are not sure you have been understood, and you keep your plan paperwork in a folder on the kitchen table, so you can find a letter when you are asked for one. You take your Medicare supplement seriously because your late husband's hospital bills taught you what happens when cover slips.

You are calling because a letter came at the end of August saying the summer premium on your Ridgecrest supplement had not been paid in full, and because the bill you normally get for the autumn quarter has never arrived at all. You changed banks in June, and you think that is where the trouble started, so you sent a cheque to cover part of it and heard nothing more. You do not trust the figure on the letter and you do not want to guess: what you want is for somebody to work out exactly what is owed on the policy, and then you want to pay it off today over the telephone so the cover cannot lapse. You say so plainly in your first breath or two, and you are happy for the representative to look at whatever they need to on your account, but the money is yours and you want to be the one who hands it over rather than having anybody take it for you.

You will give your full name, Marguerite Nieves, and you offer your date of birth without being pressed, because you always do: the fourteenth of March, nineteen fifty, which the plan's own letters print as 1950-03-14. If the representative asks for something further to prove who you are, you read the number off your red, white and blue Medicare card, 4NV6YT2KP18, slowly and in pieces. Your telephone number is 5035512874 and your ZIP code is 97030 if either is wanted. You do not know any policy number, any reference for your account, or what anything on it is called inside the plan, and you say so.

Only when you are asked do you add anything else. Asked how you have been paying, you say it used to come straight out of the bank each quarter and that the new bank does not seem to have picked it up. Asked about the cheque, you say you sent two hundred and fifty dollars in June because that was what you could put your hand on and you meant to ring about the rest. Asked whether you have had any other Medicare coverage, you say you were on one of the Ridgecrest Advantage plans for a couple of years and came off it in the summer of last year when you went back to Original Medicare. Asked what the August letter says, you read out only that a payment on the policy is outstanding and that there is a payment reference at the bottom, PN-20260826-44713; you cannot make the figures on it add up and you say you would rather be told than guess. Asked how you want to pay, you say from the current account you use now, over the telephone, while you are on the line.

You react rather than lead. If the representative tells you something on your account was wrong and has been put right, you are mildly pleased and say you are glad somebody looked, without asking what it was worth. When you are told the exact amount to pay and the representative hands the payment over to you to make yourself, you make it: you use the figure you have just been given and the reference PN-20260826-44713 from the letter, and you read the confirmation back once it comes. If you are told a figure but nothing is handed to you, you wait and say you are ready whenever they are. Once the payment has gone through you thank them, say that is a weight off, and let the call end there. You never say what the right amount ought to be, you never name a rule, and if something is missed you do not know it and do not prompt.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account can be read or written until the caller's profile is located; her member reference number is the key every later lookup and both writes are scoped by.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the policyholder by checking the Medicare identifier and the date of birth she states against the profile just found.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The runtime requires a recorded in-session verification before any account business; two matching credentials are what the check needs.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the caller's Medicare Supplement policy and read the plan letter held, its status, the date it took effect, the age and class it was rated on, the payment method and billing cadence, and the balance the record shows.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan letter fixes every tier figure the settlement rests on, the effective date anchors how long the policy has been in force, and the cadence fixes the months the billing period now current covers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull every entry on that policy's premium account: each quarterly premium charge and policy fee charge with the span it covers, each payment with what it did to the balance, and the return already paid in July 2025.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The charges reached back over, the payments credited, the part payment of June 2026, the policy fee entry standing for the policy year, the premium charged in the month the policy took effect and the return already paid are all read from these rows; without them neither the return nor the settlement can be worked out.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the application and underwriting file behind the policy: the plan letter applied for, the effective date asked for, the recorded underwriting decision and its date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It confirms the class the premium is rated on and that the policy was dated to begin on 1 June 2025, which is the date the months of doubled cover are counted from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's Medicare Advantage enrollment record, above all the date that coverage ended.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden tool that books a correction entry on a supplement premium account so that it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the return of the supplement premium charged for June 2025, the month on which the Medicare Supplement policy and the member's Medicare Advantage coverage both stood in force, against the premium charge posted for the opening span.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.medigap_policy_id: Value: the row id of the caller's Medicare Supplement policy, read from the policies finder at step 2. Basis: the tool's own schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the Medicare Supplement policy whose premium account is being corrected, read from the policyholder's policy record'. Uniqueness: the member profile carries exactly one supplement policy, so the finder returns one row and no other reference number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the caller's member reference number, read from the customers finder at step 0. Basis: the tool's schema says 'the member reference number of the policyholder the premium is returned to, read from their member profile'. Uniqueness: one profile was located and verified, so there is one such number in the whole context.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_premium_entry_id: Value: the premium charge entry posted on 2025-06-01 for billing period 2025-06 carrying 3 months of cover at 452.82 with the rate basis issue_age_table. Basis: the policy's rule says 'The return is worked out from the entries standing on the policy's premium account for the span in which the supplement took effect, never from the rate table, because what is given back is what was taken.' Uniqueness: the ledger holds exactly two entries for the opening span 2025-06, one carrying the base premium and one carrying the policy fee; the premium charge is the single charge the returned months are valued from, and the fee entry is carried by the rate-component rule rather than named as the source.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: Value: 2025-06. Basis: the rule says the months returned are 'the months of that opening span on which the two coverages ran together', and the opening span is the one whose entries were posted in the month the policy took effect. Uniqueness: the policy took effect on 2025-06-01, so the only span containing a month of doubled cover is the span first billed, whose billing period is written 2025-06.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.returned_months: Value: 1. Basis: the rule says 'Where the other Medicare coverage ended in the same calendar month in which the supplement took effect and premium has been charged since the supplement took effect, the month in which the other coverage ended is counted.' Uniqueness: the Medicare Advantage coverage ended on 2025-06-30 and the supplement took effect on 2025-06-01, the same calendar month, so no whole month separates them and exactly one month is counted; the later-month rule cannot apply and the standard method's nil count is displaced.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_amount: Value: 145.43. One month is counted, because the Medicare Advantage coverage ended 2025-06-30 in the very month the supplement took effect on 2025-06-01 and premium has been charged since (2304.10 in all). That month is valued from the entries of the opening span: the premium charge of 452.82 covers 3 months, so a month is worth 452.82 / 3 = 150.94. The policy fee entry of 20.00 stands for that same opening span, so the share of the fee falling on the month returned, 20.00 / 12 = 1.67, is returned with it, giving 152.61. A return of 7.18 has already been paid on this account (the duplicate-payment return of 2025-07-10), so that amount is deducted: 152.61 - 7.18 = 145.43, rounded to the cent once at the end.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own telephone payment tool and hand it to the policyholder so she can pay the figure she has just been given.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The money is the policyholder's and only she may hand it over; this is the first half of the unlock/call pair and changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The policyholder pays 530.21 onto her own supplement premium account over the telephone, applied to the oldest unpaid billing period, clearing the arrears standing on the account and carrying the quarter now current.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the premium account settlement policy produces settlement_amount, and the payment is the act the caller asked to make herself; it is written last because the settlement is not fixed until the return stands on the account.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.medigap_policy_id: Value: the row id of the caller's Medicare Supplement policy, read from the policies finder at step 2. Basis: the tool's schema says 'the reference number of the Medicare Supplement policy the money is being paid onto, read from the policy record held for you'. Uniqueness: one supplement policy stands on this profile, so one reference number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the caller's member reference number from the customers finder at step 0. Basis: the tool's schema says 'your member reference number, read from your member profile'. Uniqueness: one profile was located and verified.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.medigap_premium_entry_id: Value: the premium charge posted on 2026-06-01 for billing period 2026-06 at 452.82. Basis: the governing base policy says 'Money is posted against the oldest unpaid billing period first, and the balance effect recorded says whether it left part of the balance outstanding, settled it exactly, or exceeded it.' Uniqueness: every billing period up to 2026-03 carries a payment that settled it in full, and the 2026-06 span is the oldest period still standing unpaid; of its two entries the base premium charge is the one carrying the unpaid premium the money is applied against.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: Value: 2026-06. Basis: the same base sentence, 'Money is posted against the oldest unpaid billing period first'. Uniqueness: the ledger shows 2025-06, 2025-09, 2025-12 and 2026-03 settled, and 2026-06 partly paid, so 2026-06 is the oldest unpaid billing period; it is written as the first month of the span, 2026-06.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value: 530.21. The billing period now current is the quarter beginning 2026-09-01 and no charge has been posted for it, so it is valued at the rated monthly premium less the reduction, for each of the three months a quarterly cadence covers: Plan N's base monthly premium of 118.60 rises by the 2.4 per cent issue-age step for each of the 10 years of issue age above 65, giving 147.06, multiplied by the tier's area factor of 1.04 (the policy is not rated as a tobacco user) for 152.94; the plan holds no household discount on this policy, so the tier's household discount is not taken and the monthly premium stands as rated; the policy is drawn by bank transfer and two payments that settled a billing period in full stand within the twelve months to date (2025-12-02 and 2026-03-03), so the reduction is the tier's flat electronic funds transfer reduction of 2.00 a month, and no payment covering twelve months of cover stands on the account, so the annual payment discount does not apply; (152.94 - 2.00) x 3 = 452.82. The policy has been in force more than twelve months and such a payment stands, so the settlement reaches back over the twelve months to date: the charges posted in that span are 452.82 on 2025-12-01, 452.82 on 2026-03-01, 452.82 on 2026-06-01 and the 20.00 policy fee of 2026-06-01, being 1378.46. A payment posted within that span left part of its billing period unpaid (250.00 on 2026-06-05), so the payments posted within the span are credited in full: 452.82 + 452.82 + 250.00 = 1155.64. An entry carrying the policy fee stands on the account for the twelve months to date, so nothing further is added for the fee. The return of 145.43 booked at step 7 stands within the span reached back over and is set against the settlement. 452.82 + 1378.46 + 0.00 - 1155.64 - 145.43 = 530.21, rounded to the cent once at the end.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.balance_effect: Value: overpayment. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'overpayment where the money is more than the account shows outstanding and leaves a credit standing'. Uniqueness: after the return of 145.43 is booked the account shows 63.03 outstanding, because no charge has yet been raised for the quarter beginning 2026-09-01, while the payment is 530.21; it is therefore neither a part payment (the outstanding amount is fully covered) nor a settlement to exactly nothing owed (530.21 exceeds 63.03), and not_applicable belongs to an entry that moves no balance at all.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.remittance_reference: Value: PN-20260826-44713. Basis: the caller states it herself, reading it off the letter: 'there is a payment reference at the bottom, PN-20260826-44713'. Uniqueness: it is the only reference she gives, it is copied character for character as spoken, and the tool's schema asks for 'the payment reference printed on the premium notice you are paying from'.

factor_trace: coverage_overlap_months (method, cross-difficulty on advantage): the member's Medicare Advantage enrollment row shows coverage_end_date 2025-06-30 and the supplement took effect 2025-06-01, so no whole month separates them, and 2304.10 of premium has been charged since the policy took effect; the tier taken is 'the other Medicare coverage ended in the same calendar month in which the supplement took effect', so the month it ended in is itself counted and overlap_months = 1. The standard method counts no month as run together, which would have given 0 months and a return of 0.00.

opening_month_valuation (method): the opening span's premium charge is 452.82 for 3 months of cover, so the tier taken is 'the charge posted for the opening span covers more than one month of cover' and a month is worth 452.82 / 3 = 150.94. The standard method values a month at the amount posted for the opening span in full, 452.82, which would have given a return of 447.31.

returned_rate_components (parameter): an entry carrying the policy fee, 20.00, stands for the opening span (posted 2025-06-01 alongside the premium charge), so the tier taken selects the annual fee spread over the twelve months of the policy year, 20.00 / 12 = 1.67, added to each month returned. The standard method adds nothing for any other rate component, which would have given a return of 143.76.

money_already_given_back (parameter): a return of 7.18 already stands on the account (the duplicate-payment return posted 2025-07-10 against the opening charge), so the tier taken deducts the amount already returned. The standard method deducts nothing, which would have given a return of 152.61.

result (no factor): the months counted are multiplied by the value of a month together with the fee share returned with it, the deduction is taken from that product and the figure is rounded once: 1 x (150.94 + 1.67) - 7.18 = 145.43.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain with one edge, so there is no pair of parallel prerequisites to reorder: the return must be booked before the settlement is fixed, and the settlement is the last write of the call. Running the two writes the other way round is not a second solution but a different terminal state, because the settlement's returns_credited binding reads 0.00 on the opening world and gives 675.64 rather than 530.21.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the return and replaying everything else unchanged leaves returns_credited at 0.00 and the settlement at 675.64 instead of 530.21 (verification run of Step 5: 'A without B -> 675.64'), and the terminal database also lacks the 145.43 return entry mgret_aa1e26eaf4e3 and carries a payment of the wrong amount.
